$comment: Every stack and module the harness can install. A project chooses one or more `stacks`; each has a `language` (stacks of one language share tools), `srcDirs` (its source folders, the default answer), `detect`, a default `linter`, and the stacks it `excludes`. Each module is in a `group` (`groups`: the stacks its modules apply to, every stack when `null`); a module narrows it with its own `stacks` (stack or language names). Its files are in modules/<group>/<module>/: all/ for every stack it applies to, then <language>/, then <stack>/, a later folder replacing the same path; each is written at the same path in the project and merged with the project's edits. A module also brings: `scripts` (in package.json when the module brings the script on a `js` stack; otherwise, such as a `by.python` script even with a `js` stack chosen, the hooks run its `command` as written, its first word from `npx -y <npx>` when the script has an `npx` field), `checks` and `fileChecks` (what the hooks run, read from .claude/harness.json), `reports` (commands for audits, not run by the hooks), `settings` (merged into .claude/settings.json), `mcpServers` (merged into .mcp.json), `install` (commands, each run when one of the paths it `creates` is missing; with none, every time), `mcp` (the .mcp.json servers its install adds), npm `devDependencies` (a name, or `name@version` for packages that must match each other), and `audit` (the rule files and skill folders, at their paths in the project, that the audit skill checks existing code against). `by.<language or stack>` holds any of these fields for one language or stack, merged over the module's own for each chosen stack (language first, then stack; a `detect` in it limits the module to stacks where it matches). `{srcDirs}` in a command is the folders of every chosen stack the module applies to, or inside `by` those of its language or stack. `required` modules are always installed, `auto` ones exactly when their `detect` matches (package.json fields, or `files` that exist), and exactly one `linter` module per chosen stack that has one is. The setup skill suggests modules by `detect` and `recommended`, and asks about them by `group`, then by `category` (the kind of check). Modules are listed in the order their checks run. `renamed` maps a module's old name to its new one or ones, for projects that still list the old; a new name that applies to none of the chosen stacks is dropped.
